_comment: Weights for the deterministic keyword prescore in fetch_jobs.py.
This is a keyword match, not a judgment. It exists so the pipeline works with
no model in the loop, and so that when the agent does score a posting you have
something transparent to compare it against.
Points are additive. Title family and location take the single best match, in
array order, so the order of those two lists is load-bearing. Keywords and
penalties all apply. The total is clamped to 0 to 100.
Title 45 plus every keyword 50 plus location 12 is 107, so the clamp is
reachable on paper. It is not reachable in practice, because the keyword groups
are mutually unlikely: a real Tier 1 posting hits three or four of them and lands
in the eighties. If you ever see a run where many rows sit at exactly 100, the
clamp has started doing the scoring and the weights need cutting.
Tuned for the tiered target set in prompts/profile.md: Tier 1 deployment,
technical account management and solutions roles first, Tier 2 GTM and product
marketing next, Tier 3 product and analyst roles last, Tier 4 not sourced.
Geography is New York or remote-US, not any US city, because she is at Cornell
Tech in New York from August 2026 to May 2027. San Francisco scores 3, not 12.
Penalties are scanned against title, description AND location, which matters:
the out-of-scope penalty is written entirely in place names, so scanning only
the title and description let a London posting through with no penalty at all.
Every penalty here is a keyword heuristic and a backstop. The real filters are
in prompts/scoring-rubric.md step 0, which tells the agent to drop a non-US
posting, a start date before May 2027, and a Tier 4 engineering role outright.
Two of those the prescore cannot see at all: it cannot read a start date, and it
cannot tell a deployment role with a coding screen from one without unless the
words appear. That is what the agent is for.

title_families.label: go-to-market title
title_families._note: Below post-sales and solutions on purpose. GTM is a target she asked for, but she has not held a GTM title: the adjacency is account management, renewals, QBRs and expansion. See the cap in prompts/scoring-rubric.md, which the agent applies and this keyword prescore cannot.

keywords.label: enterprise or strategic accounts, post-sales ownership
keywords._note: One of the real positive signals. The word AI in a title is noise; this is not.

keywords.label: AI or model platform
keywords._note: Cut from 6. The word AI carries close to no signal now, so these patterns are worth a little as company-shape evidence and nothing more. What separates a real fit from a title match is the work described: enterprise accounts, post-sales, adoption, non-technical end users.

locations.label: San Francisco, not actionable while enrolled
locations._note: Only worth tracking for relationship building, and only where the company has a New York office. The prescore cannot check for a New York office, so this band is deliberately low and the agent decides. See the geography section in prompts/scoring-rubric.md.

locations.label: elsewhere in the United States
locations._note: Was 12, when the brief was any US city. It is now New York or remote-US, because she is at Cornell Tech in New York from August 2026 to May 2027 and cannot relocate to a third city mid-programme.

penalties.label: outside the United States, out of scope
coding screen, so this is the engineering flavour
penalties._note: The disambiguation that matters. Forward deployed and AI deployment cover two different jobs under near-identical titles, and some manager-titled deployment roles smuggle in a coding screen. A keyword hit cannot read a requirements section, so this is a backstop: the real rule is in prompts/scoring-rubric.md step 0b, which tells the agent to classify on the requirements and drop the engineering version entirely.

penalties.label: hard product manager title screen
penalties._note: She has no PM title on record, so a hard years-as-a-PM screen makes the role low-probability whatever the fit. Deprioritise, do not drop: the agent caps it and flags the screen risk in the rationale.

penalties.label: requires existing US work authorization with no CPT or OPT accommodation
penalties._note: F-1. See the hard constraints in prompts/profile.md. The agent drops these outright; the prescore can only push them down.
patterns: must have permanent us work authorization
must be authorized to work in the united states without sponsorship
